html:
The Arameans were a Semitic speaking people of Syria and upper Mesopotamia, known from about 1100 BCE. The map shows them from 1500 to 700 BCE.

After the Late Bronze Age collapse they spread across Syria and founded small kingdoms, the strongest of them Aram-Damascus (Damascus). Others settled in Babylonia. They fought often with Israel and with Assyria, which conquered their kingdoms in the 700s BCE and deported many of them.

Their lasting gift was their language. Aramaic, written in an alphabet taken from the Phoenician alphabet, spread with deported people and traders until it was the common language of the Near East. The Assyrian, Babylonian and Persian empires used it for government. Jesus spoke Aramaic, and its later form, Syriac, became a major language of Christian writing. The square Hebrew script and the Arabic script both grew from Aramaic writing.
